memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: That day the Lord exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they stood in awe of him all the days of his life, just as they had stood in awe of Moses. — Josh 4:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God had promised in the previous chapter, "Today I will begin to exalt you," and now it happens. After the miracle at the Jordan, the people held Joshua in the same awe they had held Moses. God kept His word to His servant. What God promises, God performs.

Notice how Joshua was exalted. Not by campaigning for respect, not by demanding honour, but by faithfully following God through a great act of obedience. He simply obeyed, and God lifted him up. This is God's way. As Scripture teaches, "Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up" (Jas 4:10). The path to true honour runs through humble obedience, not self-promotion.

There is also a caution wrapped in a blessing here. The people stood in awe of Joshua — but Joshua's whole aim was to point them to God. The honour he received was meant to increase their trust in the Lord who was with him, not to make Joshua the object of their devotion. Any respect a godly leader earns should ultimately direct hearts toward God.

We follow One far greater than Joshua. Jesus humbled Himself in obedience, even to death on a cross, and "therefore God exalted him to the highest place" (Phil 2:9). The pattern is the same for all who follow Christ: the way up is down. Humble faithfulness now, exaltation in God's time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you seeking honour through self-promotion, or trusting God to lift you up in His time?
2. When you are honoured or respected, do you point others back to God?
3. How does Christ's path of humility-then-exaltation shape your ambitions?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me the way of humble obedience. I trust You to lift me up in Your time, and I ask that any honour I receive would point others to You. Amen.
